headline: power is at its highest since the winter of 2022-23, and gas eased today from Wednesday's new high
commentary: UK power spot is 198.54 £/MWh, up 10.0% since our update on 26 October, 147% above a year ago and the highest since the winter of 2022-23. Gas set another high on Wednesday, with the November contract at 248.73 p/therm, then eased 3.8% today to 239.35. That is still 2.3% above Monday and about 15% above September's peak. We have no confirmed driver for today's dip, and the storage, Strait of Hormuz and February cold-weather risks reported last week stand. The winter months again rose faster than later years: November to March are up 1.6 to 2.3% since Monday, while Winter 27 is flat at 168.00. So the step down from this winter to next widened again, to 29.0%. A 24-month contract from November sits about 2.4 p/kWh below a 12-month on a wholesale-equivalent basis, because it blends this winter with cheaper years. On the winter months alone, a 12-month contract is about 0.17 p/kWh higher than on Monday. Waiting has now cost money in all six updates since late September. The Autumn Budget does not change that. It freezes new policy costs on bills until a cost-control framework arrives with the 2027 Spending Review, but cuts none of today's levies. The electricity Climate Change Levy is frozen from April 2028, and the end of Carbon Price Support on gas-fired power from April 2028 was announced in April, so markets already expect it. Day-ahead power for Friday averages £158/MWh and never drops below £152, against £24 on Sunday. That swing is the exposure a fixed price removes.
